both are third-party-driven demand handled with the same boundary shape: map the requirement to controls, supply evidence, and leave the attestation, audit and legal determination with the party who owns it

conflict_axes.name: floor_integrity_vs_price_accessibility
conflict_axes.description: Holding a non-negotiable control floor makes every package defensible but prices out the smallest businesses, who then buy nothing or buy something worthless.
poles: hold the floor in every tier
make an entry price the smallest businesses can afford
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: narrow scope above the floor rather than below it, and treat a prospect who cannot fund the floor as a decline with a referral, not as a discount case

conflict_axes.name: useful_urgency_vs_manufactured_fear
conflict_axes.description: Real deadlines and real exposure move buyers, and the same material becomes fear-selling the moment it is used to short-circuit understanding.
poles: use the exposure picture and the deadline to drive a decision
protect the buyer's ability to decide calmly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state deadlines as scheduling facts and exposure as a client-owned range, then apply the calm-down test before accepting any signature

conflict_axes.name: honest_residual_risk_vs_competitive_reassurance
conflict_axes.description: Buyers want to hear that they will be safe, and competitors will say it; the claim discipline forbids the sentence that would win the room.
poles: state residual risk plainly
match the reassurance the buyer is being offered elsewhere
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: replace the guarantee with evidence - acceptance criteria, tested restores, named non-coverage - and let the buyer who insists on a guarantee go

conflict_axes.name: estimate_accuracy_vs_authorization_limits
conflict_axes.description: Accurate fixed-fee scoping wants verified environment facts, but nothing may be scanned or accessed before authorization exists.
poles: verify the environment before quoting
touch nothing before the signature
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: have the client export their own counts under narrow permission, state every unverified assumption in the fee, and carry the residual uncertainty in the change mechanism

conflict_axes.name: standardized_tiers_vs_client_specific_fit
conflict_axes.description: Standard packages make delivery repeatable and profitable, while every client's environment argues for one more exception.
poles: keep tiers standard
fit the package to this client
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: absorb variation through a finite add-on list with defined delivery patterns, and treat a recurring exception as evidence that a tier boundary should move

conflict_axes.name: compliance_certainty_demanded_vs_guidance_boundary
conflict_axes.description: Clients want a yes-or-no verdict on whether they are compliant or insurable, which is exactly the determination this practice must not make.
poles: give the client the certainty they are asking for
stay inside mapping and guidance
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: map controls to the obligation class, show what the stack does and does not address, and route the determination to the client's counsel, assessor, broker or insurer

conflict_axes.name: close_speed_vs_duress_protection
conflict_axes.description: The moment a buyer is most willing to sign is often the moment they are least able to evaluate what they are signing.
poles: close while the pain is fresh
slow down until the buyer can decide
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sell the short emergency engagement now and the recurring agreement later, requiring the buyer to restate tier, price basis, term and one non-coverage before signature

conflict_axes.name: revenue_now_vs_disqualification_discipline
conflict_axes.description: A structurally poor-fit client pays this month and costs delivery margin, attention and reputation for the following year.
poles: take the revenue
hold the fit screen
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decline on structural grounds only, record the reason, and re-examine the criteria when a whole segment starts failing the screen

conflict_axes.name: price_stability_promise_vs_cost_passthrough
conflict_axes.description: Buyers want a fixed price for the term while vendor licensing and labor costs move underneath the agreement.
poles: promise a stable price
keep the ability to pass cost through
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use a capped or index-tied review clause plus an evidenced vendor pass-through, and disclose both aloud at signature so the mechanism is never a surprise

conflict_axes.name: displacing_the_incumbent_vs_collaborative_positioning
conflict_axes.description: The incumbent technical person is usually the client's relative or long-time contractor, and both attacking them and ignoring them lose the deal.
poles: displace the incumbent to control the environment
position alongside the incumbent
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate general IT operations from the unowned security functions, invite the incumbent into scoping, and disqualify only when the incumbent blocks a floor control

edge_cases.description: An owner calls at night mid-ransomware, files encrypted, ready to sign anything put in front of them
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect makes contact during an active incident
edge_cases.mitigation: contract a short, separately-priced emergency stabilization engagement with its own authorization, and present tiers only after recovery when the owner can restate what they would be buying

edge_cases.description: An insurance renewal is days away and the prospect wants only the two controls the form names, at the lowest possible price
edge_cases.trigger: a questionnaire deadline drives a checkbox purchase
edge_cases.mitigation: offer the floor as the minimum sellable package, help them answer the questionnaire truthfully for whatever is actually in place, and decline rather than deploy a control partially so a form can say yes

edge_cases.description: A prospect asks for a free external vulnerability scan so they can see what is exposed before deciding
edge_cases.trigger: a sales opportunity that requires touching systems before authorization
edge_cases.mitigation: substitute the questionnaire and a client-driven walkthrough of their own consoles, and schedule any scanning inside the signed engagement with scope naming the systems and the window

edge_cases.description: The person signing has no authority over a landlord-managed network or a franchisor-run point-of-sale tenant that the stack would need to touch
edge_cases.trigger: in-scope systems turn out to be owned or administered by a third party
edge_cases.mitigation: carve those systems out of scope explicitly, name the third-party owner in the responsibility matrix, and either obtain separate written authorization from that party or exclude the systems and say so in the proposal

edge_cases.description: The owner refuses multi-factor authentication on their own account while requiring it for staff
edge_cases.trigger: the buyer rejects a floor control for themselves
edge_cases.mitigation: explain that the owner's mailbox is the highest-value account in the business, offer a lower-friction second factor, and if refusal stands, decline the engagement with the reason recorded rather than accept the exposure

edge_cases.description: The seat count used to price the deal came from the owner's memory and the directory shows materially more identities
edge_cases.trigger: verified counts contradict the counts the quote was built on
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the gate, re-quote from the verified count under the true-up mechanism, and show the client the source-system export so the correction is arithmetic rather than argument

edge_cases.description: The incumbent technical contractor is also the only person who holds the credentials the deployment needs
edge_cases.trigger: the party being displaced controls the access path
edge_cases.mitigation: agree a written access-transfer plan with the client as the requesting party, keep the framing collaborative and factual, and escalate to the owner as a scheduling issue rather than as a complaint about the incumbent

edge_cases.description: A client's largest customer demands evidence of a framework certification the practice cannot produce
edge_cases.trigger: a customer-imposed security schedule exceeds the practice's competence
edge_cases.mitigation: map which control families the tiers genuinely address, state plainly that certification requires a qualified assessor, and either scope the technical portion honestly or decline with a referral

edge_cases.description: A vendor raises license pricing mid-term on an agreement that has no pass-through clause
edge_cases.trigger: cost moves under a fixed-price agreement
edge_cases.mitigation: absorb it for the remaining term rather than breaking the agreement, raise it at renewal with the vendor notice attached, and add the mechanism to the standard template so the gap does not repeat

edge_cases.description: A competitor's flyer promises complete protection and the prospect asks you to match the promise
edge_cases.trigger: an absolute-protection claim enters the comparison
edge_cases.mitigation: decline to match, explain what the package bounds and what remains, offer the acceptance criteria and restore test as checkable evidence, and let the buyer compare specifics rather than adjectives

edge_cases.description: A tooling vendor supplies a credential-exposure report about the prospect and the practice wants to use it as a lead magnet
edge_cases.trigger: third-party exposure data becomes available before any engagement
edge_cases.mitigation: use such data only where it concerns the client's own accounts and is framed as credential hygiene with its limitations stated, never as evidence of an active compromise or as a countdown to one

edge_cases.description: A seasonal business wants the billed seat count to rise and fall every month with its staffing
edge_cases.trigger: headcount fluctuates far more than the billing cadence assumes
edge_cases.mitigation: define the count date and the reduction terms in advance, hold a monthly minimum that covers the platform floor, and price the seasonal peak as a defined add-on rather than repricing the base every month

workflow.action: Publish the defensive charter and the claim-language rules
workflow.description: Fix the service set, the refusal list and the banned absolute claims before any prospect conversation happens
workflow.gate: the sell list, the refusal list with a sayable sentence for each, and the residual-risk statement all exist and are used in the first sales conversation

workflow.action: Map the decision roles and confirm signing authority
workflow.description: Identify the economic buyer, operational sponsor, incumbent technical party and external pressure source, and who can authorize each likely in-scope system
workflow.gate: each of the four roles is named or explicitly recorded as absent, and an authorizing person is identified for every system expected to be in scope

workflow.description: Work the question sequence in operational language and play the exposure picture back in the client's own words
workflow.artifact: exposure picture written in the client's words
workflow.gate: crown-jewel systems, money-movement paths, administrator holders and stated existing controls are captured, each marked client-stated or observed, and the client confirms the playback

workflow.description: Walk the client's own operating figures across an outage-duration ladder and label the result as their estimate
workflow.artifact: client exposure band with stated assumptions
workflow.gate: every input is client-supplied or a stated assumption, the output is a range, and no external breach-cost statistic appears as fact

workflow.action: Run the permitted pre-sales gap review
workflow.description: Complete the control questionnaire and a client-driven console walkthrough under narrow written permission
workflow.artifact: gap list marked client-stated and not verified
workflow.gate: only permitted activities appear in the review record, the client operated their own systems, and the deliverable carries the not-verified label

workflow.action: Screen structural fit and decide to proceed or decline
workflow.description: Evaluate the fit signals and disqualifiers and record the decision with its deciding factor
workflow.artifact: qualification record with decision, reason and any referral
workflow.gate: the decision is recorded against the named criteria, and any decline states the reason given to the prospect

workflow.action: Compose the tiers over the floor from the control-to-loss map
workflow.description: Justify every tier boundary by a mapped difference and confirm the base tier carries the entire floor
workflow.artifact: tier sheet traced line by line to the control map
workflow.gate: each tier boundary cites a mapped difference, the base tier contains the whole floor, and the add-on list is finite with defined delivery patterns

workflow.description: Assemble licensing, platform minimums, measured labor, amortized onboarding and allocated overhead per seat and per site
workflow.gate: every component names its source, labor comes from the practice's own records, and all floor controls are costed even where a client claims to have one

workflow.action: Set the billing unit, minimum, term and change mechanisms
workflow.description: Define the countable unit in writing and attach the minimum, term, notice, true-up and escalation mechanisms
workflow.artifact: price sheet with unit definition and price mechanics
workflow.gate: the countable unit, minimum, term, notice, count date and source system are all written, and the rate traces to the cost model rather than to a competitor

workflow.action: Scope and price the hardening project
workflow.description: Derive a fixed fee from counted assets with an assumption list, a change mechanism and a separate remediation line
workflow.artifact: project scope, fee, assumptions and change mechanism
workflow.gate: the counting method is recorded, assumptions are stated, pre-existing remediation is separated, and the change approver is named

workflow.action: Agree the shared-responsibility split with the client
workflow.description: Assign every control to the practice, the client or a third party and confirm the client duties that are conditions of service
workflow.gate: no control row is unassigned, third-party-owned areas are explicit, and the client has acknowledged their duties in writing

workflow.action: Assemble the proposal and gate the handoff into deployment
workflow.description: Build the proposal with all required sections, obtain signature and authorization, then check every handoff pass condition
workflow.artifact: signed proposal, authorization and handoff package
workflow.gate: every priced line traces to a mapped control, the summary page states tier, price basis, term, duties and a named non-coverage, and every handoff condition is evidenced or the deal is held with the failing condition named

dominance_rules.rule: Written authorization dominates every technical action, every sales opportunity and every deadline
dominance_rules.rationale: acting on a system without documented authority from someone who holds it is the one failure that cannot be repaired afterwards
dominance_rules.trigger: anyone proposes to scan, log into, install on or reconfigure a prospect's system before a signed authorization covering it exists
dominance_rules.action: refuse and reschedule the activity for after signature, with no exception for quick, harmless or free work

dominance_rules.rule: The defensive charter dominates any revenue opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: the practice's entire legal and professional standing rests on being strictly defensive for authorized clients
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect asks for testing, exploitation, monitoring of a named individual, or work on a system they do not control
dominance_rules.action: decline using the charter clause, explain the boundary, and refer to a qualified party where a legitimate need exists

dominance_rules.rule: The non-negotiable floor dominates price pressure and tier design
dominance_rules.rationale: a package missing a foundation control is a liability the practice will own at the first incident, whatever the client agreed to pay
dominance_rules.trigger: a deal can only close by removing, deferring or partially deploying a floor control
dominance_rules.action: hold the floor, narrow scope above it instead, and if that fails decline the deal and record the reason

dominance_rules.rule: Honest efficacy language dominates competitive pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an absolute claim wins one deal and loses the practice's credibility at the first incident across every deal
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer asks for a guarantee or reports that a competitor has promised complete protection
dominance_rules.action: state residual risk and what the package bounds, offer checkable evidence, and never match the guarantee

dominance_rules.rule: Buyer welfare under duress dominates close speed
dominance_rules.rationale: a commitment signed by someone who cannot evaluate it is neither durable revenue nor a defensible sale
dominance_rules.trigger: the buyer is mid-incident, visibly disengaged, or unable to restate what they are buying
dominance_rules.action: contract emergency work separately and short, defer the recurring agreement past the cooling-off window, and require the buyer to restate the deal before signature

dominance_rules.rule: Truthfulness of insurance and compliance answers dominates the demand wedge
dominance_rules.rationale: a misrepresented control is what an insurer examines at claim time and what turns a helpful mapping into a harm to the client
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks for help answering yes to a control that is not fully in place, or for a verdict the practice cannot give
dominance_rules.action: refuse the phrasing, offer the work that would make the answer true, and leave the answer, the signature and the determination with the client and their own advisers

dominance_rules.rule: Verified counts dominate sales optimism at the handoff
dominance_rules.rationale: every unverified count becomes a change order, a re-quote or an unpaid overrun within the first two weeks of delivery
dominance_rules.trigger: a start date or a fee depends on an asset, identity or site count that came from recollection
dominance_rules.action: hold the gate and re-derive the count from the source system before deployment begins

dominance_rules.rule: Measured cost-to-serve dominates competitor pricing as the basis of a quote
dominance_rules.rationale: another provider's price encodes their cost structure, their scope and possibly their mistake, none of which are yours
dominance_rules.trigger: a price is being set or defended by reference to what another provider charges
dominance_rules.action: derive the price from the cost model and treat the competitor's figure as market information rather than as an input

dominance_rules.rule: The written scope dominates verbal sales commitments
dominance_rules.rationale: delivery can only execute what is written, and an unwritten promise becomes a dispute in front of the client
dominance_rules.trigger: a commitment made in a meeting does not appear in the proposal or scope statement
dominance_rules.action: write it into the scope with its cost, or withdraw it explicitly before signature

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain the signed authorization and scope statement before any technical action, including inventory pulls
anti_rework_rules.prevents: work that has to be discarded, an access dispute with a third-party system owner, and a deal that cannot be defended afterwards

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify the decision roles and per-system signing authority before designing or pricing the offer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a completed proposal signed by someone who cannot authorize half the environment it describes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the control-to-loss map before composing any tier
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tiers assembled from vendor bundles that cannot be justified when the buyer asks why a line is there, or when a renewal is questioned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the non-negotiable floor before quoting any price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a quote that is only affordable because it omits a control the practice will later have to add for free or answer for

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure cost-to-serve before setting any unit price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole book priced below the cost of delivering it, which can then only be repaired client by client

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the countable unit, the minimum, the true-up and the escalation mechanism in writing at the sale
anti_rework_rules.prevents: monthly count arguments, an unpassable vendor increase, and a renewal negotiation that starts from a dispute

anti_rework_rules.rule: Count assets from source systems before committing to a fixed project fee
anti_rework_rules.prevents: change orders in the first week of the hardening project and an argument during the client's first impression of delivery

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree and acknowledge the shared-responsibility matrix before deployment is scheduled
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a deployment that stalls on client tasks nobody agreed to own, and an incident whose cause has no owner

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write every verbal sales commitment into the proposal before signature
anti_rework_rules.prevents: delivery inheriting promises it cannot meet and having to refuse them in front of the client

iteration_protocol.trigger: deployment finds the environment materially different from the discovery playback
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the affected discovery questions, restate counts and price mechanics under the true-up, and add the missed question to the pre-sales questionnaire

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured labor minutes per seat drift away from the cost model
iteration_protocol.action: recompute cost-to-serve from current ticket data, then re-examine tier composition and where the margin floor sits

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vendor changes license price, packaging, unit basis or capability
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the cost model and the control-to-loss map, then exercise the pass-through mechanism with the vendor's own notice as evidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: an attack pattern in the wild routinely defeats a control the map credits
iteration_protocol.action: update the map's coverage and non-coverage lines, restate what the affected tier claims, and correct any efficacy language already in circulation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier or a large customer changes its questionnaire or required control set
iteration_protocol.action: re-map the questions to controls, check whether a tier boundary should move, and reissue the evidence pack clients attach

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same objection recurs and keeps losing deals
iteration_protocol.action: revise the mechanism answer, add the discovery question that should have surfaced the concern earlier, and check the pitch has not drifted toward fear

iteration_protocol.trigger: below-floor discount exceptions stop being rare
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as a pricing or qualification defect, re-examine the cost model and the fit screen, and leave the floor and the guardrails intact

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client says they did not understand the term, the price basis or a non-coverage they signed for
iteration_protocol.action: review how that deal was closed against the duress and plain-language practice, fix the summary page, and re-confirm understanding with the account

priority_rationale: The charter nodes come first because the defensive service set, the authorization precondition, the claim discipline, the no-fear doctrine and duress care govern every later choice and cannot be retrofitted once a prospect has been engaged; discovery and qualification follow because the exposure picture, the client-owned loss band and the fit screen decide whether design effort is warranted at all; offer design then converts exposure into a control-to-loss map, a non-negotiable floor and tiers; economics turns that design into measured cost, a defined billing unit, a project fee, discount guardrails and price-change mechanisms; the demand wedges and objection answers are built on top of the map so they argue from mechanism rather than fear; and proposal assembly and the handoff gate come last because they compose everything above into one signed artifact and a set of pass conditions that deployment can execute without re-selling the deal.
